identity.description:
Add the evaluation harness: pr-review eval, pr-review explain and the CI gate (D4a)

Implements D4a of TICKETS.md: the evaluation harness. `pr-review eval` runs each case of a pinned case set, scores the posted findings against golden findings, reports recall, precision, findings per case, cost per case and the spread over repeats, and gates on a baseline. `pr-review explain` shows why each finding of a record was kept or dropped. A CI workflow runs the checks on every PR and the eval gate at repeat 3 on every PR that touches `prompts/`, `src/`, `eval/`, `package.json` or `package-lock.json`.

## What landed

- The case format, `loadCases`, `casesRef`, `cloneCase`, `scripts/make-case.sh` and `scripts/fetch-cases.sh`.
- The judge role (Sonnet 5.5, effort high, no tools) in `src/config/models.ts`, `prompts/judge.md`, and the match-then-judge scorer in `src/eval/match.ts` and `src/eval/score.ts`.
- `pr-review eval` with its flags, exit codes 0, 1, 2 and 3, the report document and the baseline gate.
- `pr-review explain <record> [--format table|json]`.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, the README sections Evaluate and Continuous integration, the CLAUDE.md line, the D4b and D4c tickets, and design section 9.
- `eval/cases.json` pins the case set and `eval/baseline.json` holds the first baseline.

## The cases repo

The case set lives in the private repo https://github.com/jerridan/pr-review-cases, pinned at 31b9e32346052b5914ff0c3a23c51935f715cdab. It holds four starter cases: `fixture-off-by-one` from `scripts/make-fixture.sh`, and `pr-4-consumer-workflow`, `pr-5-tests-reviewer-checks` and `pr-6-review-body-summary` from this repo's merged PRs at the head each reviewed run saw. The principal reviewed every `golden.json` on 2026-10-16 and kept five of the seven prepared goldens: the planted bug of the fixture, the README-restating tests of PR 4, the two prompt defects of PR 5 fixed in 28c0f51, and the missing blank line in the review body of PR 6. The principal struck the stale frontmatter description of PR 5 and the design-doc line of PR 6, because a golden defines what the tool must find and neither is a finding the principal wants raised. The code-bug volume comes with D4b (ReviewBench, Martian, bug injection).

The CI eval job checks the cases repo out with the `CASES_TOKEN` secret, a fine-grained read-only token on that repo, set by the principal. The checkout keeps no token.

## The live check

`eval/baseline.json` is what that run wrote: recall 0.25, precision 0.667, margin 0.05 each. The three PR cases posted nothing in nine runs, which is the recall gap the eval now measures: each of their goldens is a finding the verifier dropped by score.

## Dependencies

`package.json` gains no `dependencies` entry and no `devDependencies` entry.

## Spec

# Spec: D4a, the evaluation harness

The harness measures a change to a prompt, a threshold or a model before it ships, as design section 8 describes. It adds the command `pr-review eval`. That command reviews a set of frozen cases several times and scores the posted findings against golden findings. It adds the command `pr-review explain`, which shows why each finding of a run record was kept or dropped. It adds a CI gate that fails when recall or precision drops past a margin. The case set lives in a separate private repo that pr-review pins.

D4a builds the harness and a starter case set from this repo. D4b adds cases from ReviewBench, Martian, bug injection into jerridan/websites and jerridan/walle, and cases derived from real records. D4c runs the five first experiments and writes the results to `docs/research/`. D4a does not change the behaviour of `pr-review run`, any prompt except the new judge prompt, or any threshold. A run record keeps the same shape: `identity.models` has the same keys as before D4a, and every record that a release before D4a wrote still passes the record schema, for `explain` and for the prior-record lookup of a later run.

## Requirements

### R1. The case format

R1.1. A case is one directory. It holds the four files in this table. A missing file makes the case invalid, except `case.json`: a directory without it is not a case, as R1.9 says.

| File | Content |
|------|---------|
| `case.json` | The case metadata. R1.2 lists the fields. |
| `repo.bundle` | A git bundle. It holds `base`, `head` and the history between them. |
| `diff.patch` | The three-dot diff from `base` to `head`, kept for a reader. |
| `golden.json` | The golden findings. R1.5 lists the fields. |

R1.2. `case.json` holds the fields in this table. The `name` field equals the name of the case directory.

| Field | Content |
|-------|---------|
| `name` | The case name. |
| `source` | One of `fixture`, `pr`, `reviewbench`, `martian`, `injection`, `record`. |
| `base` | The base sha. |
| `head` | The head sha. |
| `title` | The title of the change. |
| `body` | The body of the change. |
| `origin` | Free text that says where the case came from, such as a PR url. |
| `language` | The main language of the case. |

R1.3. The schema of `source` accepts all six values. D4a ships cases with the sources `fixture` and `pr` only.

R1.4. `git clone repo.bundle <dir>` gives a checkout in which both `base` and `head` resolve.

R1.5. `golden.json` holds `findings[]`. Each entry holds the fields in this table. `start_line` is at least 1. `end_line` is at least `start_line`.

| Field | Content |
|-------|---------|
| `file` | The path of the file. |
| `start_line`, `end_line` | The line span of the finding. |
| `category` | One of `bug`, `security`, `test`, `convention`, `docs`, `performance`, `other`. |
| `severity` | One of `blocking`, `suggestion`, `nit`. |
| `claim` | What the finding says. |
| `note` | Optional. A note for the labeler. |

R1.6. A zod schema validates `case.json` and `golden.json`.

R1.7. The harness runs the CLI against the checkout from the bundle. It does not read the content of `diff.patch`.

R1.8. A case with a missing file, an invalid schema, or a bundle in which a sha does not resolve fails the eval. The message names the case and the problem. The eval exits 2 before any model call. The eval validates every case before it starts the first run.

R1.9. A cases directory holds one subdirectory per case. `--cases <dir>` points at that directory. The eval reads every subdirectory that holds `case.json`, in name order. A subdirectory without `case.json` is not a case. A cases directory with no case makes the eval exit 2 with a message.

Accept when:

- R1.1: a test that deletes each of `repo.bundle`, `diff.patch` and `golden.json` in turn from a valid case sees exit 2 each time, with the case name in the message.
- R1.2: `case.json` with a missing field, a wrong type, or a `source` outside the six values exits 2. A `name` that differs from the directory name exits 2.
- R1.3: a `case.json` for each of the six `source` values passes validation.
- R1.4: `git clone repo.bundle` of each starter case succeeds, and `git rev-parse <base>^{commit}` and `git rev-parse <head>^{commit}` succeed in the clone.
- R1.5: a `golden.json` with an unknown `category`, an unknown `severity`, a `start_line` below 1, or an `end_line` below `start_line` exits 2.
- R1.6: the validation tests of R10.4 fail on each invalid file.
- R1.7: a test that replaces the content of `diff.patch` with other text sees the same report.
- R1.8: a bundle that lacks the `base` sha exits 2 with the case name in the message. The fake client records zero calls.
- R1.9: a cases directory with two cases and one subdirectory without `case.json` gives a report of two cases, in name order. An empty cases directory exits 2.

### R2. The cases repo and the pin

R2.1. The case set lives in a separate private repo. This spec calls it `<cases-repo>`. The principal picks the name. The proposed name is `jerridan/pr-review-cases`.

R2.2. The root of `<cases-repo>` holds one directory per case, in the R1 format, and a README that says how to add a case. A clone of the repo is a cases directory in the sense of R1.9.

R2.3. pr-review pins `<cases-repo>` in `eval/cases.json`. The file holds `{ "repo": "<owner>/<name>", "ref": "<sha>" }`.

R2.4. The CLI never fetches the cases and never reads `eval/cases.json`. The eval learns the ref of the case set from the cases directory itself: when `--cases <dir>` is the top level of a git work tree, the ref is the sha of its HEAD; otherwise the ref is null. A plain directory inside another repo's work tree, such as `eval/cases/` before a fetch, gives null and never the enclosing repo's HEAD. R6.4 and R6.5 use that ref.

R2.5. The script `scripts/fetch-cases.sh [<source>]` brings the pinned case set to `eval/cases/` for a local run. It reads `repo` and `ref` from `eval/cases.json`, and both `eval/cases.json` and `eval/cases/` are relative to the current directory, so a user runs it from the repo root. It uses `git` only; `git` finds the user's own GitHub login through the credential helper that `gh auth setup-git` installs. `<source>` replaces the repo with a url or a local path, so a test can point the script at a local git repository. When `eval/cases/` does not exist, the script clones the source there and checks out the ref. When `eval/cases/` is a git work tree, the script fetches from the source and checks out the ref in place. When `eval/cases/` exists and is not a git work tree, the script exits non-zero with a message and changes nothing. After it runs, `eval/cases/` holds one directory per case, so `--cases eval/cases` finds the cases.

R2.6. `eval/cases/` and `pr-review-eval/` are gitignored.

R2.7. CI checks out `<cases-repo>` at the pinned sha. R8.4 states how.

R2.8. Rule 4 of CLAUDE.md holds. The tool reads no token. The workflow passes the `CASES_TOKEN` secret to the checkout step only. The eval step runs with `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` alone.

R2.9. D4a seeds `<cases-repo>` with a starter set from this repo:

- The case `fixture-off-by-one` is the repo that `scripts/make-fixture.sh` builds. Its golden is the planted bug. The file is `src/stats.ts`. The start line and the end line are the line in the `PLANTED` output. The category is `bug`.
- At least three cases come from merged PRs of this repo. PR #4, #5 and #6 and the D3 PR #3 are the candidates.
- The `head` of a PR case is the commit that the reviewed run saw, not the merge commit, so each golden finding exists at `head`. The goldens of the PR cases are the findings that the principal confirmed or fixed after that run. For PR #5 the head is 2222249 and the goldens are the three findings fixed in commit 28c0f51.
- A person labels each golden by hand. The run asks the principal to review every `golden.json` before the PR opens, records the answer in `decisions.md`, and cites that entry in the PR body.

R2.10. The script `scripts/make-case.sh <repo> <base> <head> <name>` writes `case.json`, `repo.bundle` and `diff.patch` into the directory `<name>` in the current directory. It fills `name`, `base` and `head`. It takes `title` and `body` from the head commit message. It sets `source` to `pr` and `origin` and `language` to empty strings. The labeler edits these fields and writes `golden.json`.

R2.11. The run prepares the content of `<cases-repo>` as a directory in the layout of R2.2. The PR body names the path. Creating the repo on GitHub is the action of the principal. The run pushes the content to it. When the repo does not exist when the cases content is ready, the run stops and asks the principal, and the PR does not open before the push.

R2.12. The principal owns three actions, and the run asks for each at the point it is needed:

| Action | When |
|--------|------|
| Create `<cases-repo>` as a private repo | Before the cases package starts. The run pushes the content once the repo exists. |
| Create `CASES_TOKEN`, a fine-grained token with read access to the contents of `<cases-repo>` only, and add it as a secret of pr-review | Before the D4a PR's own eval job can pass. That PR changes `src/` and `eval/`, so the job runs on it. |
| Review every `golden.json` | Before the PR opens. |

R2.13. At merge, `eval/cases.json` names the real repo and a sha that exists in it, and `eval/baseline.json` holds the result of a live eval at repeat 3 on that pinned set, written by `--write-baseline`.

Accept when:

- R2.1: the README, the PR body and the spec use one placeholder or one name for the repo. No file names a different repo.
- R2.2: the prepared content has one directory per starter case and a README at its root. The README holds the steps to add a case.
- R2.3: `eval/cases.json` parses as an object with the string keys `repo` and `ref`, and `repo` matches `<owner>/<name>`.
- R2.4: `grep` finds no network call, no `gh` call and no `cases.json` read in the code of the `eval` command. A test that runs the eval on a cases directory that is a git checkout reports that checkout's HEAD sha as the ref; a test on a plain directory inside a git work tree reports null.
- R2.5: a test runs the script in a temporary directory that holds its own `eval/cases.json`, with a local git repository as `<source>`, and finds `eval/cases/` at the pinned sha, with one case directory per case. A second run after a new commit in the source and a new pin checks out the new sha in place. A run with an unknown ref exits non-zero. A run with a plain file at `eval/cases` exits non-zero and leaves it.
- R2.6: `git check-ignore eval/cases/x` and `git check-ignore pr-review-eval/x` exit 0.
- R2.7: R8.4 passes.
- R2.8: `grep -n "CASES_TOKEN" .github/workflows/ci.yml` finds the secret only in the `with` block of the cases checkout step. The eval step `env` holds `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` and no other secret. A search of `src/` finds no read of `CASES_TOKEN`.
- R2.9: the prepared content holds `fixture-off-by-one` and at least three PR cases. The golden of `fixture-off-by-one` names `src/stats.ts` and the line of `PLANTED`. `decisions.md` holds the principal's answer to the golden review, and the PR body cites it.
- R2.10: a test runs the script on the fixture repo. `git clone repo.bundle` of the output resolves both shas. `diff.patch` equals `git diff <base>...<head>` of the source repo. `case.json` holds the arguments.
- R2.11: the PR body names the url of the pushed repo, and the prepared content is at the path the PR body names.
- R2.12: the record's `decisions.md` or `escalations` holds each of the three asks and its answer.
- R2.13: `gh api repos/<repo>/commits/<ref>` exits 0 for the pinned sha, and `eval/baseline.json` has `repeat` 3 and a `cases_ref` equal to that sha.

### R3. The `eval` command

R3.1. The command is `pr-review eval --cases <dir> [--repeat <n>] [--baseline <file>] [--write-baseline] [--out <dir>] [--format table|json] [--tier full|fast|skip] [--judge-model <id>] [--allow-api-key] [--allow-same-judge]`. This table lists the flags.

| Flag | Meaning | Default |
|------|---------|---------|
| `--cases <dir>` | The cases directory. Required. | none |
| `--repeat <n>` | The number of runs of each case. A positive integer. | 3 |
| `--baseline <file>` | The baseline file for the gate. R6 states the use. | none |
| `--write-baseline` | Write the baseline file. R6.5 states the rules. | off |
| `--out <dir>` | The directory for every run record and the report. | `./pr-review-eval` |
| `--format table\|json` | The format of the report on stdout. | `table` |
| `--tier full\|fast\|skip` | The tier of every run. | `full` |
| `--allow-api-key` | The flag of `pr-review run` with the same name. It also applies to the judge queries. | off |
| `--judge-model <id>` | The model of the judge. An alias or an exact id, as `src/config/models.ts` resolves them. | the `judge` role default |
| `--allow-same-judge` | Allow the judge model to equal a reviewer model. R4.4 states the rule. | off |

R3.2. For each case in name order and for each repeat in order from 1, the eval clones the bundle into a temporary directory, checks out `head`, and runs the review. The runs go in sequence. The eval runs no two reviews at the same time.

R3.3. The review runs in process through the same code path as `pr-review run --base <base> --head <head> --repo <tmp> --format json --out <out>/<case>/<repeat>/`.

R3.4. The eval uses the SDK client of the program. A test gives a fake client through `createProgram(deps)`. The review queries and the judge queries use the same client.

R3.5. The description of the change comes from the `title` and the `body` of `case.json`. The text takes the same sanitizer and the same untrusted wrapper as the title and body of a pull request, and the record's `description_meta.source` is `pr`, because the case text stands in for the pull request text. The eval makes no `gh` call and no GitHub request. It makes no network request except through the SDK client.

R3.6. The tier of every run is `full`, so every case uses the same reviewer set. `--tier` overrides it.

R3.7. Each run record is a normal record under `<out>/<case>/<repeat>/`. `pr-review explain` works on it. The records are eval samples.

R3.8. A run that exits 1, or that throws, is a failed repeat. The report lists it and its metrics are null. The eval still finishes every other run. The eval exits 1 when any repeat failed.

R3.9. A usage error exits 2. These are usage errors: no `--cases`, a `--repeat` that is not a positive integer, a `--format` outside the two values, a `--tier` outside the three values, and `--write-baseline` without `--baseline`.

R3.10. This table lists the exit codes of `eval` and `explain`. The exit codes of `run` do not change. A case whose `.pr-review/` config is invalid makes its run exit 1, which is a failed repeat under R3.8.

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| 0 | The command ran and, for `eval`, the gate passed or did not run. |
| 1 | A failed repeat, or a run error. |
| 2 | A usage error, an invalid case, or a configuration error such as a judge model equal to a reviewer model. |
| 3 | The gate failed. |

R3.11. When a failed repeat and a failed gate happen in one eval, the exit code is 1. The report still holds `gate`.

Accept when:

- R3.1: `pr-review eval --help` lists every flag in the table, with the defaults.
- R3.2: a test with two cases and `--repeat 2` finds four record directories and four runs, and a fake that records the order of calls shows no overlap between two runs.
- R3.3: a test runs `pr-review run --tier full` and `pr-review eval --repeat 1` on one checkout with one fake script. The two records are equal except for `identity.repo`, `identity.started_at`, `identity.description`, `identity.description_meta`, and the timing fields.
- R3.4: a test gives only a fake client. The test makes no real SDK call.
- R3.5: `identity.description` of each record contains the `title` and the `body` of the case, `description_me

findings.claim: The inline Node script loads `fs` with `require`, and CLAUDE.md rule 1 forbids `require`.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `node --input-type=module -e` with `import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";`, as ci.yml does.
findings.explanation: CLAUDE.md rule 1 says: use `import` and `export`, and never use `require`. The cases-pin step in ci.yml uses `node --input-type=module` with `import` for the same job.

findings.claim: renderExplainTable holds its own copy of the column-padding code of `columns()` in src/eval/report.ts.
findings.suggested_fix: Put one column-padding helper in a shared module, and use it in both files.
findings.explanation: The same change has the same padding code in two modules. A shared helper keeps one copy.

findings.claim: The description says fetch-cases.sh uses git only, but the script runs node to read the pin file.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the description and the README to say that the script also needs node, or read the pin without node.
findings.explanation: The script needs node as well as git, which the claim does not say.

findings.claim: The workflow uploads every eval run record as an artifact, so content from the private cases repo becomes downloadable by anyone who can read pr-review's artifacts.
findings.suggested_fix: Upload only report.json, or confirm the repo is private and set a short retention-days.
findings.explanation: Run records contain descriptions, file span text and findings from the private case set, which leak through artifacts of a repo with wider read access.

findings.claim: The path where writeBaseline throws during an eval (a null mean with no failed repeat) and the eval exits 1 has no CLI-level test.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an eval CLI test with --write-baseline and a fake that posts no finding. Assert exit 1, the message on stderr, and that no baseline file exists.
findings.explanation: A unit test checks that writeBaseline throws, but no test checks the exit code 1 and the stderr message of the eval in that case.

findings.explanation: The judge tests call scoreRecord with the raw fake client, not the recording client of a run, so neither new branch runs in any test.

Anyone with read access to pr-review can then download that content. The leak is real only if pr-review is more widely readable than the cases repo, and I couldn't tell that from the code. The starter cases also come from this repo's own history, so the exposure is limited until private cases are added.

quotes: # Upload the report and every record, also after a failed eval.
escalated.rationale: The workflow does upload every record from the private case set as an artifact. Whether that leaks anything depends on whether pr-review is public, and nothing in the repo says either way. The starter cases also come from pr-review's own PRs and fixture, so most of that content is not secret anyway. The gap is real but conditional and of limited value; setting a short retention would be a reasonable hardening step.

finding.suggested_fix: Add an eval CLI test with --write-baseline and a fake that posts no finding. Assert exit 1, the message on stderr, and that no baseline file exists.

finding.claim: The new judge guards in run.ts (the early return in withRoleOverrides and the throw in runRole) have no test.
finding.evidence: if (role === "judge") throw new Error("A run does not make a judge query.");
finding.suggested_fix: Add a test for each guard, or remove a guard that cannot be reached.
finding.explanation: The judge tests call scoreRecord with the raw fake client, not the recording client of a run, so neither new branch runs in any test.

quotes: if (role === "judge") throw new Error("A run does not make a judge query.");
first.rationale: The guards are new and no test reaches them: the judge tests call scoreRecord with the raw client, and the run uses the recording client only for review queries. They are defensive type-narrowing checks, so the missing test has little value.

quotes: if (role === "judge") throw new Error("A run does not make a judge query.");
escalated.rationale: The claim is correct: no test covers either judge guard. Both guards are mainly there to narrow QueryRole to Role for the type checker. Run code never issues a judge query, and runRole throws before withRoleOverrides runs, so a public-API test cannot reach either guard. A missing test for that kind of code has little value.

finding.claim: The CLI test 'keeps the judge cost out of cost_usd' fails for the same defect as the smaller metrics test with the same name.
finding.evidence: "keeps the judge cost out of cost_usd",
finding.suggested_fix: Keep the CLI test for the judge call through the eval command only. Rename it to that behaviour, or drop the cost assertion from it.
finding.explanation: test/eval-metrics.test.ts checks the same split of costs at a smaller scope, so the CLI test adds only the proof of the judge wiring.

quotes: "keeps the judge cost out of cost_usd",
first.rationale: The finding says the CLI test "fails for the same defect" as the metrics test, but nothing fails. The metrics test with the same name exists, but the CLI test also checks end-to-end judge wiring, `judge_calls`, `recall` and the report-level judge totals. Overlapping assertions at two levels are normal, so the finding is a weak redundancy remark.
